crossRefs.note: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye will no more see good.
I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
(For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days on earth are a shadow.)
“Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
“Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.
Behold, you have made my days hand widths. My lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely every man stands as a breath.”
As for man, his days are like grass. As a flower of the field, so he flourishes.
For the wind passes over it, and it is gone. Its place remembers it no more.
What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,
withdraw your hand far from me, and don’t let your terror make me afraid.
Oh spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go away and exist no more.”

translations.web: Aren’t my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, that I may find a little comfort,
translations.bsb: Are my days not few? Withdraw from me, that I may have a little comfort,
translations.kjv: Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
translations.asv: Are not my days few? cease then, And let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
